texts.preamble: Shiv Prasad Gupta vs The State Of M.P. on 16 November, 2017 1 Criminal Revision No.1782/1999 [Shivprasad Gupta Vs. State of M.P. and another] High Court Of Madhya Pradesh Principal Seat Jabalpur Single Bench: Hon. Shri Justice G.S. Ahluwalia Criminal Revision No.1782/1999 .........Applicant: Shivprasad Gupta Versus .........Respondents: State of M.P. and another Shri Shribhan Sahu, Counsel for the applicant. Shri Yogesh Dhande, Public Prosecutor for respondent/State. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Date of hearing : 16/11/2017 Date of order : 16/11/2017 Whether approved for reporting : Order
texts.facts: The necessary facts for the disposal of the present Criminal Revision in short are that on 26-5-1995, the Food Inspector, S.P. 2 Criminal Revision No.1782/1999 [Shivprasad Gupta Vs. State of M.P. and another] Dubey inspected the shop of the applicant and purchased 3 packets of vermicelli from the shop of the applicant. The packets were sealed on the spot and Panchnama was prepared. Sample was sent to the Public Analyst. The remaining two packets were deposited in the office of Local Health Authority. The applicant did not produce any receipt of purchase of the packets of vermicelli and he also did not disclose the name of the shop from where he had purchased vermicelli. The Public Analyst found the vermicelli adulterated. The permission for prosecution was obtained and thereafter complaint was filed for prosecution. Shiv Prasad Gupta vs The State Of M.P. on 16 November, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83627577/ 1 Challenging the conviction and sentence, it is submitted by the Counsel for the applicant that the Food Inspector had no authority and jurisdiction to take the samples. The independent witnesses have not supported the prosecution case. The report of the Public Analyst is vague. The provisions of Section 11(1)(a), 11(4) of the Act have not been complied with. The applicant was not supplied the copy of the report of Public Analyst as a result of which the applicant was deprived of his valuable right of getting the vermicelli re-examined by Central Food Laboratory. texts.arguments: Per contra, it is submitted by the Counsel for the State that the Food Inspector has been duly appointed by the State Govt. and he was appointed for the entire Division and he had collected the samples within his jurisdiction. The applicant neither produced the receipt nor disclosed the name of the shop from where he had purchased the vermicelli, therefore, he is not protected. The copy of the report of Public Analyst was supplied to the applicant and inspite of that, he did not exercise his right under Section 13(2) of the Act. It is next contended by the Counsel for the applicant that he had purchased the vermicelli from the market and since he is not the manufacturer, therefore, he is protected. The submission made by the Counsel for the applicant cannot be accepted for the simple reason that the S.P. Dubey (P.W.1) has stated in his examination-in-chief that the applicant was asked to produce the receipt of purchase of vermicelli, but he did not produce the same. He also did not disclose the name of seller. Even during the trial, the applicant has not produced any receipt to show that from where he had purchased the vermicelli. Under this circumstance, it cannot be held that the applicant was not the manufacturer or was entitled for protection. As the applicant did not produce the 5 Criminal Revision No.1782/1999 [Shivprasad Gupta Vs. State of M.P. and another] receipt of purchase of vermicelli, as well as did not disclose the name of the seller, therefore, it cannot be said that there was any warranty in favor of the applicant. Thus, the applicant is not entitled for protection under Section 14 of Act. Even the applicant did not disclose the name of the vendor as required under Section 14-A of the Act. It is next contended by the Counsel for the applicant that the copy of the report of the Public Analyst was not sent and hence, he has been deprived of his valuable right of re-examination of the sample by Central Food Laboratory. The contention made by the Counsel for the applicant is misconceived and is hereby rejected. S.P. Dubey (P.W.1) has specifically stated that after filing the complaint, a copy of the report of the Public Analyst was sent to the applicant by registered post on 15-5-1996 Ex. P.20. It is further submitted by the Counsel for the applicant that since the independent witnesses did not support the prosecution story, therefore, the solitary evidence of S.P. Dubey (P.W.1) is not reliable.
